research_concepts: opponent next-possession points per possession (PPP) after a play type
methodological_questions: Is the opponent's next-possession PPP after play X large enough to drive an AVOID label, and how is AVOID operationally defined?
Do own-sequence lagged outcomes add explanatory value beyond the opponent's next-possession PPP?
Are AVOID labels derived from the same next-possession outcome being tested, which would make the test circular?
What exposure and sample sizes are needed for stable per-play-type PPP, and how is multiplicity controlled?
Do the labels used for play types match expected league distributions, and how reliable are they across seasons and teams?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type label backfill verification (observed_result: 'Final: FAIL'). PNR 28.7% FAIL (band 20-28%); PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL; 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL; PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; temporal PASS; team identity FAIL; 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams. Auto failure mechanism recorded as C_artifact. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. Sample: 921,514 possessions. Validation: no validation recorded.

Superstar sequential suppression: a specific opponent play type on the preceding possession is hypothesised to suppress each star's next-possession PPP relative to baseline. PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222, n=52). Other top cells were small (TRANSITION for A. Davis -0.058; POST_UP for N. Jokic -0.075). Recorded failure mechanism: E_unclear. No multiplicity correction; n_after 32-95 for several PUTBACK cells against thousands of baseline possessions. 30 stars, min n_after=30.

Superstar suppression profiles, including Q5c sequential triggering. Verdict recorded as 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'. Examples: Jokic after opponent POST_UP 1.1271 (-0.0675, SE ±0.0500, n=480); Curry forced POST_UP -0.209. Rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control. An OTHER artifact is flagged in the document. Failure type recorded as E_unclear.

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels (ORL-DET G1). Hypothesis: NBA matchup/PBP fields can label on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) at usable rates. DET: 10 of 67 on-ball possessions labelled (14.9%); ORL: 2 of 60 (3.3%). switches_on was not populated. Verdict recorded as failed_gate; failure mechanism A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilling play-type labels and checking them against expected league distributions and team identities, where many labels were proxy-calibrated.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact. Label distributions failed for PULL_UP (2024-25 shares near 0-2% for many teams) and PNR (team-level overrun in 3100 games), and team identity failed. The record links the failure to label or classification error (LIM:label_or_classification_error).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing star next-possession PPP suppression to a specific opponent play type on the preceding possession.
failed_approaches.why: Mechanism recorded as E_unclear. No multiplicity correction; several PUTBACK cells rest on n_after of 32-95. The record flags DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY as a risk. It is not a hypothesis test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking the rank-1 opponent-play suppressor per star and testing sequential triggering.
failed_approaches.why: Mechanism recorded as E_unclear. Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control, and an OTHER artifact was flagged. Verdict inconclusive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage from the NBA matchup and PBP fields.
failed_approaches.why: Mechanism recorded as A_unanswerable. Label rates were very low (14.9% and 3.3%), and the switches_on field was not populated. Verdict failed_gate. Linked limitations are small sample and label or classification error.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels derived from the play-by-play have shown reliability problems in this project: one backfill audit over 921,514 possessions failed its checks, with PULL_UP shares near zero for many teams in 2024-25 and 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated (FAM:SF-APPA-030).

Opponent play types on the preceding possession have been tested for suppression of star next-possession PPP. The effects found so far are small, noisy and not multiplicity-controlled (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022).
Some defensive-scheme labels from the matchup feed cannot be produced at usable rates with the current fields (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
PNR PPP of 0.948 passed a check in FAM:SF-APPA-030, so the outcome side of the derived records has at least one passing check.
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved defines AVOID, sets a threshold for what counts as an AVOID label, or reports a test of the opponent next-possession PPP against such a threshold.
No retrieved record tests own-sequence lagged effects on AVOID labels.
No retrieved record validates the labels used for the question (validation status is NOT_RECORDED in each record).
The retrieved star-level suppression results do not show whether the effect operates at the play-type level or whether it drives labels.
No retrieved record reports a valid, multiplicity-controlled effect size for opponent next-possession PPP.
own_inferences: If AVOID is defined from the opponent's next-possession PPP, the test is circular (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL). The question cannot be answered until AVOID is defined from information available before the outcome.
The 2024-25 PULL_UP and PNR label problems mean any play-type-level estimate for those seasons is at risk of label error, which biases the play-type contrasts.
The star-level PUTBACK results are probably too small and too noisy to support a league-wide AVOID threshold.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on the question date (complete from 2026-06-21), so they cannot serve as a holdout. The 2025-26 regular season is complete and can serve as one.
Own-sequence lags must be built only from possessions before the one being predicted, otherwise leakage is possible.
uncertainties: The AVOID label definition, its threshold and its inputs are not in any retrieved record.
Retrieval returned four records, and none addresses AVOID or own-sequence lags directly. The coverage of the project's history is therefore uncertain.

The status of FAM:SF-APPA-030 is recorded as inconclusive while its observed result states 'Final: FAIL' with the C_artifact mechanism. This conflict is reported as recorded and has not been resolved.
Exposure counts per play type and opponent combination are unknown.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 label pipeline matches the one that produced the failing backfill is not established.
The conditional frequency of AVOID under the project's label rules is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that labels built from this play-by-play have failed validation (FAM:SF-APPA-030), that star-level opponent-play effects are underpowered and uncontrolled for multiplicity (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022), and that some label families cannot be populated (FAM:SF-APPS-058). These findings lower the testability of the question as posed and require the label to be validated before any effect is attributed to it. The decision moves from a plain test to do_not_proceed as posed, with a conditional minimum viable test.

blocking_constraints.text: AVOID is not defined in the retrieved records. If it is defined from next-possession PPP, the test is circular.
Play-type labels failed validation in FAM:SF-APPA-030 (PULL_UP near zero for many 2024-25 teams, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated). FAM:SF-APPS-058 failed its gate for defensive-scheme labels.
The star-level PUTBACK cells have n_after of 32-95 (FAM:SF-APPA-050), too small for stable per-cell estimates.
Across play types and stars, no multiplicity control was applied in FAM:SF-APPA-050 or FAM:SF-APPM-022.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work in this project addresses adjacent questions only. FAM:SF-APPA-050 and FAM:SF-APPM-022 test whether specific opponent play types on the preceding possession suppress star next-possession PPP. Their results are small, uncontrolled for multiplicity and not a valid test of AVOID. FAM:SF-APPA-030 shows that the play-type labels used by the project have failed validation. FAM:SF-APPS-058 shows that some defensive-scheme labels cannot be produced at usable rates. No retrieved record tests whether the opponent's next-possession PPP after play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels, and none tests own-sequence lags against AVOID.

risks.text: If AVOID uses the next-possession outcome, the test is circular. The label must be defined before outcomes are observed.
Labels failed validation in FAM:SF-APPA-030 and the defensive-scheme labels in FAM:SF-APPS-058 are sparse. Misclassified play types bias play-type PPP contrasts.
Per-play-type and per-star opponent-next cells are small (n_after 30-95 in FAM:SF-APPA-050), so estimates are unstable.
Rare play types and specific opponent-then-own combinations may have too few possessions for stable estimates, and the record does not give exposure counts.
Many play-type and star contrasts were run without correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022). Any AVOID threshold screen will have the same problem.
Score margin, period, clock, lineup, pace and team strength can all affect both play selection and next-possession PPP.
Own-sequence lags or opponent next-possession fields built from the full game record can include information from after the decision point.
Play-type definitions and league-wide PPP changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26. FAM:SF-APPA-050 flags drift as a risk.
Opponent-next effects can appear through selection on game state, so a placebo sequence is needed to separate real sequencing from artifact.
The derived possession graph is built from the play-by-play, so possession boundaries and PPP attribution errors would propagate into the test.

design.estimand: Conditional on a pre-registered AVOID definition that does not use the next-possession outcome, the difference in opponent next-possession PPP after play X versus matched baseline possessions, and the incremental effect of own-sequence lags. The estimate is conditional on the label passing validation.
design.unit: Defensive possession following an offensive play X in the derived possession graph, with the opponent's next-possession PPP as the outcome.
design.sample: Derivation: 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Holdout: 2025-26 regular season, complete from 2026-04-13. Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial on 2026-06-19 and complete only from 2026-06-21.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum of 1,000 possessions per play type and a target SE of 0.03 PPP for the contrast. Compute by bootstrap resampling at the game level. Report the achieved SE for each cell and drop cells below the minimum.
design.controls: Game state (score margin, period, clock), lineup and pace, team and opponent strength, with random effects for team and game. Own-sequence lags are built only from possessions before the predicted one. Label validation is a precondition: backfill and team-identity checks must pass on the derivation seasons before any effect is estimated.
design.falsification: Placebo opponent-next sequences (play X assigned to a shuffled or non-adjacent possession) and within-game shuffle of the sequence. The effect must vanish under both. Compare AVOID-labelled and non-labelled play types on the holdout season.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the set of play types and stars. Control the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg across play types and stars. Report all cells, including those that fail.
design.decision_rule: AVOID is supported only if the pre-registered effect exceeds a pre-specified PPP threshold, with the 95% CI excluding the threshold on the 2025-26 holdout, the placebo effects vanish, and label validation passes. If the label validation fails, the result is reported as an artifact. If the CI spans the threshold, the result is uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as of 2026-06-19: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) as holdout; 2025-26 playoffs excluded because they are partial on the question date.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
